title: Jeff Nippard is WRONG about Natty or Nots.
summary: He agrees with Jeff Nippard that natty-or-not videos waste viewers' time, then traces the format's history (Blaha, Vegan Gains, Philion, Doucette, MPMD) to argue it was born from jealousy and greed, never hurt a fake natty, and pushes young naturals toward drugs. He then accuses Jeff's natural vs enhanced muscle-gain video of doing the same thing under scientific cover, and of misusing GVS and Alex Leonidas as examples of a natural limit.
claims: Jeff is right that natty-or-not videos are a waste of life: whether someone is natural or not, comparing yourself to them is pointless
Natty-or-not videos started around 2014; the five main producers were Jason Blaha, Vegan Gains, Philion, Greg Doucette and More Plates More Dates, and each grew big off the format
The format was born from jealousy and greed, not a wish to protect naturals; Blaha, himself enhanced, started it out of envy of young fake natties' success
Vegan Gains used natty-or-nots to push veganism, calling out meat eaters while overlooking obvious PED use among vegan bodybuilders
PEDs, name-dropping and drama are the holy trinity of virality on fitness YouTube
Philion went from 40-80 views per upload to over 4 million with one David Laid natty-or-not, despite having no knowledge of drugs or lifting
Natty-or-not videos never got a fake natty cancelled; Mike O'Hearn has been called out for 20 years and still thrives, because call-outs are free publicity
Natty-or-nots mostly just shift viewers through a savior-complex cycle: one influencer calls out another, gains the audience, then exploits it
Fake natties are here to stay: as long as drugs exist people will take them and lie about it for clout
Everyone is fascinated by PEDs because we are all in it for muscle; he was obsessed with PED content himself around 2016
The new trend of teenagers openly documenting their cycles is even worse than fake natties
Natty-or-nots are gossip disguised as information, lifters' own tabloids; viewers are like a soccer mom buying a celebrity magazine while pretending it's research
Greg Doucette blew up after switching to natty-or-nots about three years ago, and now calls physiques you can reach in two years of training enhanced
Telling young lifters that ordinary physiques need drugs convinces them they can't look good natural, so natty-or-nots push more naturals onto PEDs
More Plates More Dates draws people in with PED curiosity, convinces them they can't look good natural, then sells supplements such as test boosters (placebo at best) and co-owns a TRT clinic
Ask yourself whether you ever learned anything useful about programming, technique or exercise selection from MPMD
Only the creator and the subject of a natty-or-not benefit; the millions of viewers get nothing
Knowing how much muscle naturals vs enhanced lifters can gain in 10 years has no effect on what you will look like, and can talk you out of starting at all
Jeff's video repackages natty-or-nots with science: PED talk plus name-dropping, while keeping the moral high ground
Saying physique tells you nothing about advice quality because drugs build size is a fallacy; once drugs are taken out, a natural's physique does say something about their methods
Using GVS and Alex Leonidas as examples of the natural limit is dishonest, since both are still clearly growing and reject the idea
Showing teenagers that naturals gain 20-40 lb of muscle in 10 years while enhanced lifters gain that in under a year will convince them staying natural is a waste of time
Consequences matter more than intentions, so creators are responsible for how their content affects young viewers
